disease_data.name: Bronchiectasis

initial_presentation.chief_complaint: chronic productive cough with recurrent infections

patient_demographics.appearance: chronically ill, frequent coughing with sputum production

physical_exam.general: chronically ill appearing, frequent productive cough

respiratory.auscultation: coarse crackles at bases, rhonchi, squeaks, wheezes

cardiovascular.auscultation: may have loud P2 if cor pulmonale

hrct_chest.result: bronchial dilation >1.5x adjacent artery, lack of bronchial tapering, signet ring sign

chest_xray.result: increased markings, tramlines, ring shadows, may be normal

sputum_culture.result: Pseudomonas, H. influenzae, S. pneumoniae, NTM (non-tuberculous mycobacteria)

immunoglobulin_levels.result: low IgG, IgA, or IgM if immunodeficiency

teaching_points: HRCT with bronchial dilation >1.5x adjacent artery is diagnostic
Signet ring sign: dilated bronchus next to pulmonary artery
Treatment: airway clearance, antibiotics for exacerbations, treat underlying cause
Pseudomonas colonization indicates more severe disease
Massive hemoptysis may require bronchial artery embolization
key_features: Chronic productive cough with copious sputum

disease_data.name: Community-Acquired Pneumonia

respiratory.palpation: increased tactile fremitus over affected area

chest_xray.result: lobar consolidation in right lower lobe with air bronchograms

blood_culture.result: positive for Streptococcus pneumoniae in 20% of cases

teaching_points: CURB-65 score determines outpatient vs inpatient management
Streptococcus pneumoniae is most common cause of CAP
Empiric antibiotics should cover typical and atypical pathogens
Chest X-ray may lag clinical improvement by several days
Parapneumonic effusion requires thoracentesis if moderate or large
key_features: Acute onset of cough, fever, and dyspnea
Crackles and bronchial breath sounds on examination

disease_data.name: Pulmonary Edema (Cardiogenic)

patient_demographics.appearance: appears severely distressed, sitting upright, gasping

past_medical_history.heart_failure: yes, known systolic or diastolic dysfunction

vital_signs.blood_pressure: elevated 180/100 or low if cardiogenic shock

physical_exam.general: severe respiratory distress, diaphoretic, sitting bolt upright, tripod position

respiratory.inspection: labored breathing, use of accessory muscles
respiratory.auscultation: bilateral crackles, diffuse rales from bases to apices, wheezing (cardiac asthma)

cardiovascular.auscultation: S3 gallop, tachycardic, possibly murmur if valvular

physical_exam.extremities: cool if low output, peripheral edema, pitting

chest_xray.result: bilateral infiltrates in butterfly pattern, Kerley B lines, cephalization, cardiomegaly, pleural effusions

bnp_or_ntprobnp.interpretation: Heart failure present, excludes non-cardiac causes

ecg.result: may show LVH, ischemia, arrhythmia, previous MI
ecg.interpretation: Identifies precipitating factors or underlying heart disease

troponin.result: may be elevated if ischemic etiology

echocardiogram.result: reduced EF if systolic dysfunction, diastolic dysfunction, valvular disease

abg.result: severe hypoxemia, respiratory alkalosis initially, then acidosis

teaching_points: BNP >500 or NT-proBNP >900 indicates heart failure
Treatment: oxygen, IV diuretics, nitrates, consider CPAP/BiPAP
Identify and treat precipitating cause (ischemia, arrhythmia, infection)
Distinguish from ARDS: BNP low in ARDS, normal heart size
LMNOP mnemonic: Lasix, Morphine, Nitrates, Oxygen, Position (upright)

disease_data.name: Pleural Effusion

patient_demographics.appearance: appears mildly dyspneic, may lean toward affected side

physical_exam.general: comfortable at rest or mildly dyspneic

respiratory.inspection: decreased chest wall movement on affected side
respiratory.auscultation: decreased or absent breath sounds, egophony above effusion

cardiovascular.inspection: JVD if CHF, no JVD if other causes

chest_xray.result: blunting of costophrenic angle, meniscus sign, if large: opacification of hemithorax

ct_chest.result: fluid collection, identifies underlying lung pathology

pleural_fluid_analysis.result: protein, LDH, glucose, pH, cell count, cultures, cytology

teaching_points: Light's criteria distinguishes transudate from exudate
Transudate: CHF, cirrhosis, nephrotic syndrome (treat underlying cause)
Exudate: infection, malignancy, PE (requires further workup)
Thoracentesis indicated if >1cm on lateral decubitus film or unknown etiology
Complicated parapneumonic effusion requires chest tube drainage
key_features: Dullness to percussion at lung base
Blunted costophrenic angle on chest X-ray

disease_data.name: Interstitial Lung Disease (Idiopathic Pulmonary Fibrosis)

initial_presentation.chief_complaint: progressive shortness of breath and dry cough

patient_demographics.appearance: appears chronically ill, tachypneic, uses accessory muscles

primary_symptoms.dyspnea: yes, progressive, initially with exertion then at rest

associated_symptoms.no_fever: yes, absence of fever is typical

exposures.occupational: asbestos, silica, coal dust, metal dust

respiratory.auscultation: bilateral fine inspiratory crackles (velcro crackles) at bases

cardiovascular.auscultation: may have loud P2 if pulmonary hypertension, RV heave

physical_exam.skin: may have findings of connective tissue disease

hrct_chest.result: usual interstitial pneumonia (UIP) pattern: subpleural, basal predominant reticular opacities, honeycombing, traction bronchiectasis
hrct_chest.interpretation: Characteristic findings allow diagnosis without biopsy

pulmonary_function_tests.result: restrictive pattern: reduced FVC and TLC, FEV1/FVC ratio normal or increased, reduced DLCO

chest_xray.result: bilateral reticular or reticulonodular opacities, reduced lung volumes, honeycombing if advanced

abg.result: hypoxemia, increased A-a gradient, normal or low CO2

autoimmune_panel.result: ANA, RF, anti-CCP if connective tissue disease

surgical_lung_biopsy.result: UIP pattern: patchy fibrosis, fibroblastic foci, honeycombing
surgical_lung_biopsy.interpretation: Gold standard but not always needed if classic HRCT

teaching_points: IPF is most common idiopathic interstitial pneumonia, median survival 3-5 years
UIP pattern on HRCT: subpleural, basilar reticular opacities with honeycombing
Treatment: antifibrotics (pirfenidone, nintedanib) slow progression but don't reverse fibrosis
Lung transplantation is only curative option
Velcro crackles (fine inspiratory crackles) are characteristic finding
key_features: Restrictive pattern on PFTs with reduced DLCO
UIP pattern on HRCT with honeycombing

patient_presentation.text: A 67-year-old M patient presents to the outpatient clinic with progressive shortness of breath and dry cough. The patient appears chronically ill, tachypneic, uses accessory muscles.

disease_data.name: Spontaneous Pneumothorax

initial_presentation.chief_complaint: sudden onset chest pain and shortness of breath

patient_demographics.age_range: 20-40 for primary spontaneous, any age for secondary
patient_demographics.appearance: appears anxious, tachypneic, tall thin habitus if primary

past_medical_history.underlying_lung_disease: COPD, cystic fibrosis, asthma for secondary

vital_signs.blood_pressure: normal or decreased if tension PTX

physical_exam.general: anxious, tachypneic, sitting upright, leaning toward affected side

respiratory.inspection: decreased chest wall movement on affected side, tracheal deviation away from affected side if tension
respiratory.palpation: decreased tactile fremitus on affected side
respiratory.auscultation: decreased or absent breath sounds on affected side

cardiovascular.auscultation: tachycardic, may be muffled if large

physical_exam.signs_of_tension: tracheal deviation, JVD, hypotension, absent breath sounds - medical emergency

chest_xray.result: visceral pleural line separated from chest wall, absent lung markings peripherally

expiratory_chest_xray.result: more apparent pleural line on expiration

ct_chest.result: clearly defines pneumothorax and any underlying blebs/bullae
ct_chest.interpretation: Gold standard, detects occult PTX, identifies blebs

ultrasound.result: absence of lung sliding, absent comet-tail artifacts

teaching_points: Tension pneumothorax is clinical diagnosis - needle decompression before imaging
Primary spontaneous PTX occurs in tall thin young males at rest
Pneumothorax >2cm or symptomatic requires intervention (aspiration or chest tube)
Recurrence rate 30-50% after first episode, higher with subsequent episodes
Avoid flying or scuba diving for 2 weeks after resolution
key_features: Decreased breath sounds on affected side
Visceral pleural line on chest X-ray
